correctness.rationale: For the complete K3 with initial effective path, self-inclusive HK averaging has gap matrix [[1,2],[2,1]]/6, so sum gap D/2^t and gap difference (u-v)(-1/6)^t while both adjacent edges stay receptive. The missing edge has confidence c0 delta^t; under strict comparison it appears exactly when (2delta)^t>D/c0. This proves nonactivation at and below delta=1/2 and the precise floor+1 crossing when above; the Perron stationary left vector (2,3,2)/7 yields the limit, while the contrast mode determines the exact finite consensus value after activation. Two agents cannot have permanently missing edge yet equal limiting opinions under positive initial confidence. Four independent exact-fraction 15-step trajectories checked boundary and activated cases; the unrestricted proof is algebraic.

value.rationale: The same-limit but unreceptive-edge effect is a published qualitative phenomenon. A sharp minimal-three-agent, open-parameter construction with exact half-decay transition and first activation time resolves the smallest natural configuration and exposes a singular distinction between limit consensus and finite-time consensus. The theorem is explicitly sector-specific, not a claim of a global network threshold.
